blocks.text: PROPHET IN THE DAYS OF JOSIAH (ZEPHANIAH 1:1) · TWO KINGDOMS
Zephaniah. He proclaimed “the great day of the LORD” on Judah and the nations, and a humble remnant who would sing.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Josiah
BOOK
Zephaniah
HOW THE WORD CAME
The book opens with the word of the LORD coming to him, and gives his line back four generations: son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hizkiah.
THE CALL
How the word came

The book opens with the word of the LORD coming to him, and gives his line back four generations: son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hizkiah. Whether Hizkiah is King Hezekiah is an open question (below). Zephaniah 1:1
Much of the book speaks in the LORD's own voice (“I will utterly consume”, “I will search Jerusalem with candles”). Zephaniah 1:2 Zephaniah 1:12
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Josiah
KING OF JUDAH
Josiah
THE MESSAGE
The word in its main themes
The day of the LORD is near
“The great day of the LORD is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly”
Zephaniah 1:14 (KJV) →
“That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress”
Zephaniah 1:15 (KJV) →
Against the worship in Jerusalem
“I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil.”
Zephaniah 1:12 (KJV) →
Seek the LORD, ye meek
“Seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the LORD’s anger.”
Zephaniah 2:3 (KJV) →
The nations around, and Nineveh
Jerusalem's leaders
A remnant, and singing
“The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.”
Zephaniah 3:17 (KJV) →
THE WORD TO …
To whom the word was spoken
TO JUDAH AND JERUSALEM
“I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem”
Zephaniah 1:4 (KJV) →
TO THE PHILISTINES
“Woe unto the inhabitants of the sea coast, the nation of the Cherethites!”
Zephaniah 2:5 (KJV) →
TO MOAB AND AMMON
“Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah”
Zephaniah 2:9 (KJV) →
TO THE ETHIOPIANS
“Ye Ethiopians also, ye shall be slain by my sword.”
Zephaniah 2:12 (KJV) →
TO ASSYRIA AND NINEVEH
“This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me”
Zephaniah 2:15 (KJV) →
TO THE DAUGHTER OF ZION
“Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem.”
Zephaniah 3:14 (KJV) →
THE BOOK
The book of Zephaniah
1 Heading Zephaniah 1:1
2 The day of the LORD on Judah Zephaniah 1:2–2:3
3 Against the nations Zephaniah 2:4–15
4 Woe to Jerusalem Zephaniah 3:1–8
5 A pure language, a remnant, a song Zephaniah 3:9–20
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture says nothing of him beyond the first verse of his book. Zephaniah 1:1
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Yes, the king
Ibn Ezra, as reported by the Jewish Encyclopedia (1904); Keil (1868); G. A. Smith (1898)

Keil reasons that a line traced back four generations points to a well-known ancestor: Hezekiah “must have been a celebrated man, and that in all probability the king of that name is intended.” Smith: “Zephaniah's great-great-grandfather Hezekiah was in all probability the king.” Zephaniah 1:1 [12][45][43]
Possible but not certain
A. B. Davidson (1896); S. R. Driver (1891)
Davidson: “The royal descent of Zephaniah, though not certain, is supported by plausible grounds.” Driver only reports that “it is supposed by some” that the king is meant.[46][3]
No
Abravanel, as reported by the Jewish Encyclopedia (1904)
The Jewish Encyclopedia says that Abravanel “rejected this identification.”[43]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 3
Zephaniah 1 Zephaniah 2 Zephaniah 3
PASSAGES · 1
Zephaniah 1:1–3:20
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no call, no story and no death for Zephaniah; all it tells of him is in Zephaniah 1:1.
He is a different man from Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah, the priest of Zedekiah's day (Jer 21:1; 2 Kgs 25:18).
The New Testament does not quote Zephaniah by name.
